definition: Vergence is a visual and oculomotor process involving coordinated eye movement control. In this packet, it is treated as part of the systems that support eye movements and related attentional control.

reasons: The packet does not define what “vergence” is (e.g., it does not describe it as a “visual and oculomotor process involving coordinated eye movement control”). It only mentions “brain areas involved in vergence and oculomotor control” without giving a definitional description.

The claim that the packet treats vergence as “part of the systems that support eye movements and related attentional control” is only indirectly supported (the text discusses cortical regions involving vergence/eye movements and mentions attentional control tasks), but the key definitional component (“Vergence is…”) is not supported.

The packet supports that vergence is discussed alongside eye movements and oculomotor control, but it does not define vergence as a “visual and oculomotor process” or as part of “systems that support eye movements and related attentional control.”

The attentional-control claim overgeneralizes the source: the packet says light exposure affected cortical areas associated with “attentional control tasks such as oculomotor control,” not that vergence itself is an attentional-control process or system.
